lessonRef.subject: mathematics
lessonRef.unitTitle: Mathematical Habits and Place Value to One Million
lessonRef.focus: choosing a rounding place and estimating to judge reasonableness
lessonRef.title: Applied problem solving: choosing a rounding place and estimating to judge reasonableness

sections.title: Instructional examples
sections.directions: This example shows the kind of reasoning the problem below asks for.

steps: The nearest multiples of 10,000 are 580,000 and 590,000.

sections.title: Guided practice
sections.directions: Talk through what the problem is asking before you compute.

items.prompt: You solved a multi-digit problem, but the answer has way more digits than makes sense. What should you do?
choices: Estimate the answer first, then compare your exact answer to the estimate to check for a place-value mistake.
Multiply every number in the problem together.
Skip the problem without trying it.
Guess an answer and move on to the next problem.

sections.title: Independent practice
sections.directions: Work on your own. Show the steps that produced each answer.

items.prompt: A problem could be solved more than one way. What should you do before picking a method?
choices: Multiply every number in the problem together.
Guess an answer and move on to the next problem.
Think about which method fits the numbers best, then explain why you chose it.
Skip the problem without trying it.

items.prompt: You read a word problem with several numbers in it and are not sure where to start. What should you do first?
choices: Guess an answer and move on to the next problem.
Restate the problem in your own words and identify exactly what question is being asked.
Multiply every number in the problem together.
Skip the problem without trying it.

sections.title: Extension and challenge
sections.directions: Write out the reasoning in full sentences. A correct answer with no justification does not count here.

items.responseExpectation: Give the result and the reasoning that produced it. Show enough work that someone else could check each step.
Give the result and the reasoning that produced it. Show enough work that someone else could check each step.
